title: Re-ranking (Cohere/Cross-Encoders)
summary: Use a stronger query-document relevance model on a bounded shortlist before expensive generation consumes the evidence.
overview: Re-ranking is a second retrieval stage that scores candidate passages against the query after an inexpensive first-stage search. A cross-encoder jointly processes query and passage, allowing richer interactions than separately embedded vectors. Hosted reranking services provide a similar architectural role, with service-specific limits and contracts.

The reranker cannot recover a relevant document absent from the candidate set. First-stage recall and second-stage ordering must therefore be measured separately. Its score is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability that a passage is correct or authorized. Long passage truncation and unsupported languages can distort ranking even when the service returns successfully.

production.poc: Start with a fixed retrieval shortlist and labeled relevance judgments to isolate whether reranking improves order.
production.production: Production budgets candidate count and passage length, sets timeouts, and defines an acceptable fallback to first-stage ranking.
production.scale: At scale, batch compatible scoring work, monitor language and domain slices, and version reranker changes alongside retrieval evaluations.

components.name: Candidate retriever
components.role: Produces a diverse high-recall shortlist under trusted filters.

components.name: Passage normalizer
components.role: Preserves title, relevant text, and provenance within reranker limits.

components.name: Cross-encoder service
components.role: Scores each query-passage pair using joint attention or an equivalent ranking model.

components.name: Selection policy
components.role: Chooses top evidence while controlling redundancy and source diversity.

components.name: Ranking evaluator
components.role: Tracks recall, ordering quality, latency, and downstream answer support.

flow.title: Retrieve candidates
flow.description: Collect a bounded shortlist from dense, sparse, or hybrid retrieval.

flow.title: Prepare pairs
flow.description: Attach the question to each passage and preserve essential headings and source identity.

flow.title: Score relevance
flow.description: Run the reranker under a deadline and record its model version.

flow.title: Select evidence
flow.description: Sort by relevance while removing duplicates and respecting document diversity requirements.

flow.title: Apply answerability rule
flow.description: Do not force an answer when even the best candidates lack sufficient evidence.

flow.title: Record outcome
flow.description: Compare accepted evidence and eventual answer support against labeled evaluation examples.

useCase.title: Finding the relevant experimental protocol
useCase.situation: A research assistant searches approved laboratory protocols and historical method notes.
useCase.problem: Many passages share assay terminology, but only a few address the requested sample preparation conditions.
useCase.requirement: Rank passages by the specific experimental question before drafting an evidence-linked summary.
useCase.architecture: Hybrid retrieval supplies candidates and a domain-evaluated cross-encoder selects the most relevant sections.
runtime: The query retrieves passages mentioning the assay family.
Reranking promotes the protocol containing the requested sample condition and demotes unrelated validation notes.
useCase.failure: If the reranker times out, the service uses a tested retrieval-only mode and exposes reduced evidence confidence where appropriate.
useCase.impact: Track relevant-passage rank and unsupported-answer rate alongside added latency; fluent summaries do not prove that ranking improved.

tradeoffs.benefit: Improves the chance of retaining relevant evidence.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires more compute and domain evaluation.

failures.detection: Correct passages score poorly only at longer lengths.
failures.recovery: Split or select relevant windows while preserving headings and provenance.

failures.detection: Top results repeat nearly identical passages.
failures.recovery: Apply diversity constraints after scoring and evaluate their relevance cost.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting reranking to fix missing candidates
mistakes.fix: Improve first-stage recall before adjusting the reranker.
Evaluate each supported language and domain slice.

whenToUse: Use when retrieved candidates are relevant but poorly ordered.
Use before expensive generation over a limited context.
Use for queries requiring fine distinctions among similar passages.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when first-stage recall is the dominant failure.
Avoid unbounded reranking of the whole corpus.
Do not rerank unauthorized candidates as a substitute for filtering.
